thesis: A deleveraging PBM and employer-health franchise with ROIC of 12.6% and an 11.58% FCF yield trades below its own 5-year minimum P/E and EV/EBITDA, where the price implies a revenue decline that raised 2026 guidance does not show.
reason: Same evidence as the last review plus fresh sector policy risk: cheap on every own-history multiple with strong cash conversion, but thin margins, 2027 rebate and GLP-1 headwinds and the CMS audit proposal keep it below the buy bar. Held at the conviction-3 size it was already trimmed to.

triggers.text: TTM ROIC falls below 10%, giving up most of the five-year improvement from 8.8% to 12.6%.
TTM operating margin falls below 3.5%, under the FY2025 five-year low of 3.7%, showing rebate reform or medical cost pressure is compressing profitability structurally.
TTM FCF margin falls below 2.0%, well under the current 2.9%, signalling cash generation and buyback capacity are deteriorating.
Net debt/EBITDA rises above 2.5x (1.87x TTM now), reversing the deleveraging.
